assumptions: frame members weighed as thin rods: density x area x length at the member centre
friction coefficient 0.8 (assumed; the load case usually gives mu)
suspension arm bushings 3 kN/mm across the pivot axis (assumed: within passenger-car arm bushings, 1.7 to 5.0 kN/mm, no UTV value; the design has no bushing_radial_stiffness)
suspension arm bushings 0.5 kN/mm along the pivot axis (assumed: a little above passenger-car arm bushings, 0.23 to 0.46 kN/mm, no UTV value; the design has no bushing_axial_stiffness)
tie rod 10 kN/mm along its length, rack held (assumed, no source; the design has no tie_rod_stiffness)
K&C tables from the design's suspension hardpoints_mm, with their compliance from the bushings and the tie rod; longitudinal forces taken at the contact point

tyre forces: Magic Formula 6.1 with the coefficients of the 205/60R15 91 V, 2.2 bar (passenger car) tyre (H. B. Pacejka, Tire and Vehicle Dynamics, 3rd edition (2012), Appendix 3: the reference tyre's MF-Tyre parameters; not checked against the book). Not a measured UTV tyre: only the shapes of the passenger car tyre's curves are used, scaled to this vehicle: nominal load 1584 N (the mean static wheel load), R0 = the wheel radius, and at each wheel's static load the peak friction = mu and the slopes at zero slip = the stiffnesses K2 took (design or defaults above); held at the coefficients' nominal inflation pressure (no pressure terms, so nothing is extrapolated to a low-pressure tyre)

centres of pressure at the centroids of the part boxes and wheels projected on the side and front planes (along x always; the areas and the side centre's height only where the design does not give them) (assumed)
